source_user: Advanced cluster case multi-node NCCL-111: A multi-node NCCL job hangs only at larger world sizes. Produce a falsifiable diagnosis and rollback plan. Variant 111 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: test rank mapping, interface selection, topology, NIC affinity, rendezvous, firewall and ports, timeout logs, communicator formation, reduced-world baselines, and network counters. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Treat the hang as an observation, not proof of cause. Assumptions: the collective, message shapes, placement, launcher, software versions, and failing world sizes can be reproduced; platform-specific facts must be measured. Record exact NCCL/CUDA/driver/framework/container/launcher versions, node/GPU inventory, rank-to-device and TP/PP/EP mapping, topology, selected interface and NIC/NUMA affinity, MTU/routes, InfiniBand/RoCE mode, rendezvous endpoint, authorized firewall/port policy, timeout settings, and synchronized clocks. Redact endpoints, tokens, and credentials.

Falsifiable hypothesis for variant 111: a scale-triggered rank, transport, or worker failure is hidden by the collective timeout. Hold workload, versions, placement, message sizes, and timeout policy constant. Binary-search the minimum failing world size and repeat each condition at least three times. Compare a known-good reduced-world run, the first failing world size, and a matched full-world run; change one factor per trial. Collect synchronized per-rank logs with the last completed collective, rank/world size, timestamps, communicator-formation status, selected transport/interface, and timeout stack; correlate these with topology, NIC/fabric counters (errors, drops, retransmits, congestion), CPU/GPU/NIC utilization, memory, file descriptors, and rendezvous/port connectivity, all with units and timestamps.

Interpretation: support the hypothesis only if the failure reproduces at the same threshold and the changed factor alters the outcome without a competing change. Check rank ordering, interface/NIC affinity, topology and routes, rendezvous and authorized ports, communicator formation, transport configuration, resource limits, and worker exits before changing settings. A passing reduced-world test is not proof for the full world size; distinguish model-domain expectations from measured evidence and list unknowns.

Safety and rollback: use read-only diagnostics first and only authorized isolated canaries. Do not disable authentication/firewalls globally or expose ports. Stop if another workload is affected, errors increase, a worker becomes unhealthy, or the run exceeds the agreed timeout/error budget. Revert temporary placement, environment, routing, or transport changes, terminate the canary cleanly, collect final redacted logs/counters, and verify the baseline workload and cluster health. Claim improvement only after repeated matched trials with confidence intervals or clearly reported variability; otherwise mark evidence_required.

Treat the hang as an observation, not proof of cause. Assumptions: the collective, message shapes, placement, launcher, software versions, and failing world sizes can be reproduced; platform-specific facts must be measured. Record exact NCCL/CUDA/driver/framework/container/launcher versions, node/GPU inventory, rank-to-device and TP/PP/EP mapping, topology, selected interface and NIC/NUMA affinity, MTU/routes, InfiniBand/RoCE mode, rendezvous endpoint, authorized firewall/port policy, timeout settings, and synchronized clocks. Redact endpoints, tokens, and credentials.

Falsifiable hypothesis for variant 120: the selected interface/NIC path or its reachability differs for one or more added rank pairs. Hold workload, versions, placement, message sizes, and timeout policy constant. Binary-search the minimum failing world size and repeat each condition at least three times. Compare a known-good reduced-world run, the first failing world size, and a matched full-world run; change one factor per trial. Collect synchronized per-rank logs with the last completed collective, rank/world size, timestamps, communicator-formation status, selected transport/interface, and timeout stack; correlate these with topology, NIC/fabric counters (errors, drops, retransmits, congestion), CPU/GPU/NIC utilization, memory, file descriptors, and rendezvous/port connectivity, all with units and timestamps.
